questions.answer: She will be queen one day

questions.question: In 1995, Ceuta and Melilla passed their statutes and became… what?
hints: They aren't quite autonomous communities.
They're the only two of their kind in Spain.
Their name puts “city” together with the word used for Spain's self-governing communities.
questions.fun_fact: Until 1995, Ceuta was part of the province of Cádiz and Melilla part of the province of Málaga.

questions.question: On “Atrapa un millón”, players spread stacks of banknotes across the answers. What were the trapdoors in the studio for?
questions.answer: To swallow the money on wrong answers
wrong_answers: To let the host pop up by surprise
To hide the questions of the show
To shoot confetti when someone won
hints: Carlos Sobera hosted it on Antena 3.
The more you got wrong, the fewer banknotes you had left.
After each question, the floor opened under the incorrect answers.
questions.fun_fact: The format comes from a British game show called “The Million Pound Drop”.

questions.question: Look at this golden eagle. Where does it usually build its nest in Spain?
questions.answer: On a rocky cliff in the mountains
wrong_answers: In a hole in the ground
In the sand of a beach
On the roof of a house
hints: It likes to have a good view.
It's very high up and far from people.
Think of the crags of the Pyrenees.
questions.fun_fact: A golden eagle's nest can be more than 2 m (6.5 ft) wide, because the pair makes it bigger year after year.
